Al Darraq Introduces Advanced Well Integrity System to UAE Oil & Gas Market

Al Darraq Industrial Solutions, a leading oilfield equipment provider, has announced the launch of its new WellGuard 360 platform in the United Arab Emirates, marking a significant development in the rapidly evolving Oil & Gas Services & Equip sector. The product was unveiled at the Abu Dhabi Energy Forum on Tuesday, where regional stakeholders gathered to discuss innovations shaping the future of upstream operations.

The WellGuard 360 platform integrates real-time monitoring with predictive analytics, aiming to enhance well integrity management and reduce maintenance costs for operators across the UAE. According to Al Darraq, the system leverages proprietary sensor technology and artificial intelligence to deliver early warnings for potential well integrity issues, allowing operators to address anomalies before they escalate.

“Ensuring the long-term integrity of wells is a top priority for our clients,” said Tarek Al Mahri, Chief Technology Officer at Al Darraq Industrial Solutions. “With the WellGuard 360, we are providing the tools necessary to transition from reactive maintenance to proactive asset management, supporting the region’s commitment to maximizing hydrocarbon recovery while meeting the highest safety and environmental standards.”

The UAE, which is among the world’s top oil producers, has maintained a strong focus on deploying advanced technologies to optimize resource extraction. The government’s support for digital transformation in the energy sector has spurred local and international service providers to introduce a new generation of solutions.

Industry analysts welcomed the launch, highlighting the growing importance of well integrity management in the region’s mature fields. “Aging infrastructure and the drive to extend the economic life of wells mean that technologies like WellGuard 360 are becoming increasingly relevant,” said Noor Khaled, energy analyst at Middle East Petroleum Insights. Khaled noted that spending on well integrity and monitoring solutions across the Gulf Cooperation Council is projected to grow by 7% annually through 2027.

Representatives from the Emirates Oilfield Contractors Association praised Al Darraq’s initiative, emphasizing the role of domestic innovation in supporting UAE’s strategic energy objectives. “Local development of advanced oilfield solutions strengthens the entire value chain and enhances the UAE’s position as a technology hub for the sector,” said association chairperson Ahmad Al Mutairi.

Al Darraq indicated that pilot trials of the WellGuard 360 are already underway with two major national operators, with commercial deployments expected in the second half of 2024. The company plans to expand the offering to other markets in the Gulf region next year.

The launch of WellGuard 360 underscores the increasing sophistication of oilfield services in the UAE as operators seek to balance productivity, cost-efficiency, and regulatory compliance in a competitive global landscape.
